1.mascotDialogue: No comparisons anywhere in this algorithm, beta — none at all! Just repeatedly asking 'which bucket does this digit belong in' and gathering the buckets back up in order, digit by digit.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 10's backward loop, beta — that is what keeps radix sort stable! Processing the original array from the end preserves the relative order of elements that share the same digit. Small detail, big deal.

3.mascotDialogue: 170 and 90 both land in bucket 0 for this pass, beta — and their relative order, 170 before 90, is preserved! That is stability doing its job, quietly, across every single pass.

4.mascotDialogue: This is why the loop direction matters, beta, even though it looks like a harmless stylistic choice! Radix sort's correctness across multiple passes depends on each individual pass being stable, not just correct all on its own.
